body:
## Module 2 in two minutes

**The artisan tax** is what you pay every time you re-brief an AI on material that hasn't changed — your voice, your standards, your org's shape, retyped per conversation, forever. The fix is the **context pack**: the durable briefing for one workflow, written once, attached always.

**Three bins, one discipline.** Durable-and-impersonal material lives in the pack: a gold-standard example, the definition of done, your voice rules, the team glossary. Run-specific material — this week's notes, this quarter's verbatims — arrives fresh and leaves with the run. And anything identifying a person never becomes infrastructure: packing it converts a one-time judgment call into a standing condition nobody re-decides.

**Context rots.** The org brief goes stale at the next reorg, and stale context fails the way fluent output always fails — confidently. Date-stamp every pack item, review the fast-aging ones monthly, prune what nobody's needed in two cycles. When a run goes wrong because the pack was wrong, fix the pack before you fix the output.

### The boundary rule

People data must never become infrastructure. Sensitive material may enter a single run as fresh input, under that run's judgment — it never lives in packs, instructions, or anything a future conversation can see.

**The full module adds** the instructions-vs-knowledge design rule, the hands-on pack build in your organization's tools, a twelve-item sorting exercise, and capstone stage 2: the pack for your own workflow.
